memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: You must not sacrifice the Passover in any town the Lord your God gives you except in the place he will choose as a dwelling for his Name. There you must sacrifice the Passover in the evening, when the sun goes down, on the anniversary of your departure from Egypt. - Deut 16:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God insisted that the Passover be kept in one appointed place, the place He would choose for His Name. This may sound restrictive, but it was actually protective. It kept worship united and pure, guarding the people from scattering into private, invented forms of religion, each family doing whatever seemed right to them.

Worship was not something they designed to suit themselves. It was a response to God on His terms. There is deep humility in coming to God the way He asks, rather than the way we prefer. Our natural hearts love to shape worship around our own comfort and convenience.

For us who live on this side of the cross, the "place" has changed. Jesus told the woman at the well that a day was coming when true worshippers would worship the Father in the Spirit and in truth, not tied to one mountain or temple (John 4:21-24). Christ Himself is now the meeting place between God and us. Yet the principle stands, we come to God through the way He has appointed, through His Son, and not through paths of our own making. Are you worshipping God on His terms or trying to bend Him to yours?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you tend to worship God on His terms or your own?
2. What does it mean that Christ is now our meeting place with God?
3. Where might you be shaping faith around your comfort?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I come to You through Jesus, the way You have appointed. Teach me to worship You in spirit and in truth. Amen.
